verses.1: A psalm. A song for the dedication of the temple. Of David.
verses.2: I praise you, LORD, for you raised me up and did not let my enemies rejoice over me.
verses.3: O LORD, my God, I cried out to you and you healed me.
verses.4: LORD, you brought me up from Sheol; you kept me from going down to the pit.
verses.5: Sing praise to the LORD, you faithful; give thanks to God's holy name.
verses.6: For divine anger lasts but a moment; divine favor lasts a lifetime. At dusk weeping comes for the night; but at dawn there is rejoicing.
verses.7: Complacent, I once said, "I shall never be shaken."
verses.8: LORD, when you showed me favor I stood like the mighty mountains. But when you hid your face I was struck with terror.
verses.9: To you, LORD, I cried out; with the Lord I pleaded for mercy:
verses.10: "What gain is there from my lifeblood, from my going down to the grave? Does dust give you thanks or declare your faithfulness?
verses.11: Hear, O LORD, have mercy on me; LORD, be my helper."
verses.12: You changed my mourning into dancing; you took off my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness.
verses.13: With my whole being I sing endless praise to you. O LORD, my God, forever will I give you thanks.

notes.text: For the dedication of the temple: a later adaptation of the psalm to celebrate the purification of the temple in 164 B.C. during the Maccabean Revolt.
Healed: for God as healer, see also Psalm 103:3; 107:20; Hosea 6:1; 7:1; 11:3; 14:5.
Sheol... pit: the shadowy underworld residence of the spirits of the dead, here a metaphor for near death.
Complacent: untroubled existence is often seen as a source of temptation to forget God. Cf Deut 8:10-18; Hosea 13:6; Proverb 30:9.
in the stillness of Sheol no one gives you praise; let me live and be among your worshipers. Cf Psalm 6:6; 88:11-13; 115:17; Isaiah 38:18.
